notes: Chosen hook: '5 FIRMS, 3 SITES / NORDIC AI BID' (option 0). Scores: clear in 2 seconds 7 (readable at once, but 'bid' for what is left open; the kicker 'EUROPE AI · INDUSTRY' helps); curiosity 6 (two numbers raise 'which firms, which sites', but no tension or surprise); concrete number or name 9 (5 and 3, both in the source and the facts list); promise kept 9 (slide 02 names exactly five firms and the bid; the sites slide names Oulu, Iru and Valmiera and says Sweden has no site yet, so '3 sites' is accurate and nothing is promised about approval or funding); reader stake 2 (industry bid, no effect on readers; acceptable because the other four criteria are strong). Overall 7, a pass but not a high one. Hook types are honest: option 0 'number' is a number hook, option 1 'rivalry' is a rivalry hook, option 2 'claim' is a loose claim. No option is reader-impact, and hook_pick_reason has an honest 'No reader-impact hook:' sentence saying the article states no effect on ordinary readers. Comparison: option 1 (NOKIA VS TELEKOM) is punchier but overstates, since heise says Telekom is only 'among the most prominent' competitors and the consortium is five firms, not Nokia alone; the slides would not keep a head-to-head promise. Option 2 (EUROPE'S AI BET GOES NORTH) has no number or name and is vague, with 'bet' implying a scale the slides do not claim. Option 0 is the best of the three. Minor notes, not fails: (1) 'Nordic' in the headline is slightly loose because Estonia and Latvia are Baltic; the caption says 'Nordic and Baltic', so consider a 'NORTHERN' or 'NORDIC-BALTIC' wording only if it fits the render. (2) The cover comma after 'SITES' sits tight against the second line but is legible.
